title: Did Les Paul multitrack before this?
summary: They argue when Les Paul's multitrack recordings were made.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Was he impatient with himself? Not only did you invent Super sax, you invented Les Paul with that gig.
He did that a long time before this.
I don't think it was much before 1955.

I'm sure it was. I heard about Les doing that--I met Les, I used to go out jamming with him in the early Herbie Fields days, we used to go out to these black clubs in Brooklyn and play, and I'd say within ten years after that I heard about him doing things in his own studio, within ten years--fifteen tops. That would put it close to those days, a few years before. I would say it would put it 1950.
I'm not sure I wouldn't argue that, but this is not the appropriate place.
My memory is so bad, Bill, that I could be very wrong.
I think he was somewhere in the fifties. That would have been in the days of Johnny Ray and that kind of pop music and that was in the fifties, say the early-
I'm trying to remember when I heard about him doing that when I was out in California.

I don't mean to take away from his originality, his invention of that thing, but I think "How High The Moon" which was the big record made on those multiple tracks of his, that was in the mid fifties.
He did some of them with his wife, she did the multiple voices. Well, I hope one of us is right.
Either you invented him or he invented you.
Whoever was responsible for my dream.
